scope: Port the already proven SM0 two-authority handoff semantics onto the exact accepted P6 product baseline without merging historical research lineage. First bounded product slice: two authorities A/B behind the accepted Edge Gateway path, two graphical clients, one real P6 player/outpost composition, WARM target preparation, A->B->A authority transfer with stable identities, OperationId/input continuity, exactly one canonical writer, unchanged client gateway endpoint, canonical Item Graph/Construction/persistence continuity, stale-source fencing, restart/reconnect convergence, and a deterministic fault matrix.
required_outputs: Production SM1 authority-domain adapter built from current P6 main only
A/B authority handoff state machine with one-writer fencing
WARM read-only target reconstruction using existing P6 canonical state
Gateway-preserving route pivot with no client server-endpoint disclosure
Graphical A->B->A scenario with two clients and unchanged player identity
Fault matrix covering pre-commit death, post-commit response loss, stale source return, target failure, duplicate/reorder, concurrent crossings
Fresh review, verification and exact-head evidence before checkpoint proposal
stop_conditions: Implementation requires a second Item Graph, Construction truth or persistence owner
Implementation requires Gateway to decide ownership or gameplay truth
Implementation requires direct client connection to simulation-server endpoints
Implementation requires changing NX transport/reconciliation foundation rather than consuming it
Implementation requires wholesale merge of SM0 or research/SM1 history
More than one active authority can authorize the same canonical aggregate
Exact accepted P6 base cannot be proven
risk_reasons: Touches player authority, route continuity and canonical write fencing
Must preserve persistent P6 composition through mid-flight failure and replay
A split-brain or duplicate commit would corrupt canonical gameplay truth

design_brief.problem_statement: P6 is accepted and supplies persistent shared gameplay plus gateway-ready identities and operation continuity, while SM0 separately proved two-authority handoff. The product lineage still lacks a production A<->B handoff composed with current P6 owners.
design_brief.current_behavior: A P6 player remains under one active authority. WARM/SHADOW is read-only evidence, but no current-main product path performs an authority ownership switch.
design_brief.desired_behavior: The player crosses A<->B without respawn, logical/entity identity change, client gateway rehome, duplicate operation, Item Graph split, Construction split or persistence divergence; exactly one authority is active at every canonical mutation point.
design_brief.selected_design: Port only SM0 handoff semantics into a fresh SM1 adapter layer over P6. Source ACTIVE freezes, target WARM reconstructs and validates, the canonical ownership transition is the linearization boundary, source retires, target activates with a higher authority epoch, and retries converge exactly once. Gateway remains routing-only.
alternatives_considered: Reconnect client directly to target authority
Allow both authorities to write during overlap
Create an SM1-private world/player persistence layer
expected_risks: Lost/duplicated operations across ambiguous commit response
Identity or input-sequence reset at route pivot
non_goals: No Gateway rehome in the ordinary handoff path
validation_plan: L1 composition against real P6 identity/ledger/admission/outpost modules
L2 two-authority process scenario through existing Gateway path
Two graphical clients A->B->A with invariant event trace
Full world regression plus independent review and verification
design_brief.why_selected: It minimizes new truth: P6 remains the product state owner set, SM0 supplies only proven transfer semantics, and Gateway/NX remain transport owners.

notes: Control candidate only. Runtime mutation remains forbidden until this post-P6 reconciliation is independently reviewed, integrated into main, the single mutation lease is rotated to SM1, and a Director DISPATCHED event is committed.
